findings.checklist_item: - [ ] Reconcile the pre-scan help-token rule: state that for NON-nested commands a `--help`/`-h` in ANY position before a `--` terminator is served as usage (preserving the bug-b8de fix), and only nested families (bridge/audit) require a LEADING help token — and clarify how that squares with the 'free-text --help later in argv remains data' clause.
evidence: Plan Approach: 'a first `--help`/`-h` token after the spelling'
Plan Approach: 'Free-text `--help` later in argv remains data/handler input as today.'

_help_route.wants_help scans ALL tokens before `--` and documents bug b8de: '`rebar create task --help` used to fall through to the create handler, which consumed --help as the positional title and created a placeholder ticket'; help_requested reserves the leading-only rule for _NESTED_FAMILY (bridge/audit) only.
probe_rebar.py:587-590 expects `create --help` to show usage and create nothing
findings.finding: The plan's description of the help pre-scan's token handling is internally inconsistent and, read literally, understates the required scan: it says the pre-scan handles 'a first --help/-h token after the spelling' and that 'Free-text --help later in argv remains data/handler input as today,' but the goal actually requires serving --help/-h in ANY position before a `--` terminator for non-nested commands (the bug-b8de fix so `rebar create task --help` shows usage and does NOT create a placeholder ticket), reserving the leading-token-only rule for nested families (bridge/audit).
findings.location: Approach — 'The lexical pre-scan handles ... a first --help/-h token after the spelling'; and 'Free-text --help later in argv remains data/handler input as today.'
scenarios: An implementer wiring the pre-scan to match the literal 'first token after the spelling' would let `rebar create task --help` (help flag NOT first) fall through, reintroducing bug b8de (placeholder-ticket creation).
findings.suggested_fix: Rephrase to: 'For non-nested commands the pre-scan honors a `--help`/`-h` token in any position before a `--` terminator (preventing bug b8de); nested families (bridge, audit) treat only a LEADING `--help`/`-h` as the family usage request, deferring child `--help` to argparse. A `--` terminator, or a help flag inside a nested child, leaves later `--help` as handler data.'
